elements.element: Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Sections 19.1 and 19.2A expressly provide that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.

elements.element: Software and Deliverables will conform to their documentation for 12 months after delivery.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 warrants that each Deliverable will conform to its documentation for 12 months after delivery, and Section 19.2A expressly provides the same 12-month period for software.

elements.element: Services will conform to their documentation for 90 days after performance.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2A expressly warrants that Services will conform to their documentation for 90 days after performance.

elements.element: Vendor will repair or re-perform items that breach the required performance or conformance warranties.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 provides repair and re-performance only for breaches of Sections 19.1 and 19.2; it does not cover Section 19.2A. Section 19.1 covers only material service nonconformity, so the remedy does not fully apply to the unqualified 90-day service-conformance warranty in Section 19.2A.

elements.element: Vendor will replace items that breach the required performance or conformance warranties.
elements.evidence: Although Section 19.4 includes replacement, it applies only to Sections 19.1 and 19.2 and omits the unqualified 90-day service-conformance warranty in Section 19.2A.

elements.element: Vendor will provide a refund for items that breach the required performance or conformance warranties if cure is unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 provides a refund if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period, but only for breaches of Sections 19.1 and 19.2. It does not extend that refund remedy to the full Section 19.2A service warranty.

elements.element: Vendor will comply with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Section 19.3 expressly states that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law.

elements.element: Services, Deliverables, and software will contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Section 19.3 prohibits only malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor. It does not prohibit malicious code introduced unintentionally or by other sources, so it is narrower than an unqualified no-malicious-code warranty.

elements.element: Software will conform to its documentation for at least 90 days after delivery.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2A provides a 12-month software-conformance warranty, which exceeds the 90-day fallback duration.

elements.element: Services will conform to their documentation for at least 30 days after performance.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2A provides a 90-day service-conformance warranty, which exceeds the 30-day fallback duration.

elements.element: Vendor will repair or re-perform items that breach the fallback conformance warranties.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 omits Section 19.2A from its remedy cross-reference. Section 19.1 covers only material service nonconformity, leaving the unqualified service warranty in Section 19.2A without the required full repair or re-performance remedy.

elements.element: Vendor will replace items that breach the fallback conformance warranties.
elements.evidence: The replacement remedy in Section 19.4 applies only to Sections 19.1 and 19.2, not the full service-conformance warranty in Section 19.2A.

elements.element: Vendor will provide a refund for items that breach the fallback conformance warranties if cure is unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: The conditional refund in Section 19.4 does not apply to Section 19.2A, so it does not fully cover the fallback service-conformance warranty.

result.reason: The redline supplies the preferred warranty durations, professional-and-workmanlike standard, and legal-compliance warranty. It does not provide an unqualified no-malicious-code warranty. More importantly, Section 19.4 was not updated to include Section 19.2A, leaving the new unqualified service-conformance warranty without the complete repair, replacement, and refund framework. The drafting is also non-minimal because Section 19.2A redundantly repeats warranties already stated in Sections 19.1 and 19.2 and is placed after Section 19.4. Unrelated commercial terms remain effective, and the duplication does not create a direct contradiction.
